outcome: Conversion failure from epidural labour analgesia to epidural surgical anaesthesia
Requirement for change of anaesthesia technique (to spinal or general anaesthesia)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1084 parturients who underwent conversion from epidural labour analgesia to anaesthesia for caesarean delivery at three hospitals in Chengdu, China, between May 2019 and April 2020.
finding: Prolonged duration of epidural labour analgesia, particularly exceeding 8 hours, was an independent risk factor for conversion failure from epidural labour analgesia to epidural surgical anaesthesia for caesarean delivery.
